# Module `term`

term - terminal + stdin I/O module.

Interactive console I/O for TUI-style programs (a lynx-style browser): read
from stdin / keypresses, send diagnostics to stderr, flush stdout, and control
the terminal (size query + ANSI escapes). Everything crosses the runtime's
`__vyb_stdin_*` / `__vyb_eprint*` / `__vyb_term_*` functions in
`runtime/vyb_runtime.c`; the Vyb surface stays allocation/pointer-free.

Usage:
  import term::{stdin_read_line, stdin_raw_enable, stdin_raw_disable,
                eprintln, flush, term_cols, term_rows, term_clear,
                term_move_cursor, term_hide_cursor, term_show_cursor}
  line<String> = stdin_read_line()          # one line (no trailing newline)
  stdin_raw_enable()                        # single-key reads, no echo
  key<Int> = ...                            # then read raw bytes with stdin_read
  stdin_raw_disable()
  eprintln("diagnostic goes to stderr")     # never corrupts the rendered page
  flush()                                   # make stdout visible before input
  cols<Int> = term_cols(); rows<Int> = term_rows()

Stdin readers return a String (empty on EOF). The raw-mode toggles and flush
helpers return `Bool?` (absent on failure, e.g. stdin is not a TTY); the
stderr writers return `Int?` holding the bytes written, absent on error.


Put stdin in raw mode: read single keypresses without waiting for Enter, no
echo. Returns `Bool?` -- present on success, absent if stdin is not a TTY or
termios fails.

<a id="sym-stdin_read"></a>
### `stdin_read` · fn

```
stdin_read(maxlen<Int>)<String> ->
```

Blocking read up to `maxlen` bytes from stdin. In canonical (cooked) terminal
mode this typically returns one line; in raw mode it returns up to `maxlen`
keypress bytes. Returns an empty String on EOF.

<a id="sym-stdin_read_line"></a>
### `stdin_read_line` · fn

```
stdin_read_line()<String> ->
```

Blocking read of one line (until '\n' or EOF). The trailing newline is
stripped, and CRLF collapses to the bare line. Returns an empty String on EOF.
